{{Short description|Integral transform introduced in 1990}}
The '''Sumudu transform''' is an [[integral transform]] introduced in 1990 by G K Watagala.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Watugala |first=G. K. |date=January 1993 |title=Sumudu transform: a new integral transform to solve differential equations and control engineering problems |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0020739930240105 |journal=International Journal of Mathematical Education in Science and Technology |volume=24 |issue=1 |pages=35–43 |doi=10.1080/0020739930240105 |issn=0020-739X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Asiru |first=Muniru Aderemi |date=May 2002 |title=Further properties of the Sumudu transform and its applications |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/002073902760047940 |journal=International Journal of Mathematical Education in Science and Technology |language=en |volume=33 |issue=3 |pages=441–449 |doi=10.1080/002073902760047940 |s2cid=123671820 |issn=0020-739X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Zhang |first1=Jun |last2=Shen |first2=Fangyang |chapter=Sumudu Transform for Automatic Mathematical Proof and Identity Generation |date=2018 |editor-last=Latifi |editor-first=Shahram |title=Information Technology - New Generations |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-54978-1_85 |series=Advances in Intelligent Systems and Computing |volume=558 |language=en |location=Cham |publisher=Springer International Publishing |pages=677–683 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-54978-1_85 |isbn=978-3-319-54978-1}}</ref> It is defined over the set of functions <ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kılıcman |first1=A. |last2=Gadain |first2=H. E. |date=2010-06-01 |title=On the applications of Laplace and Sumudu transforms |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003210000785 |journal=Journal of the Franklin Institute |volume=347 |issue=5 |pages=848–862 |doi=10.1016/j.jfranklin.2010.03.008 |issn=0016-0032|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Watugala |first=G. K. |date=January 1993 |title=Sumudu transform: a new integral transform to solve differential equations and control engineering problems |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0020739930240105 |journal=International Journal of Mathematical Education in Science and Technology |language=en |volume=24 |issue=1 |pages=35–43 |doi=10.1080/0020739930240105 |issn=0020-739X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kapoor |first=Mamta |date=June 15, 2023 |title=Sumudu Transform for Time Fractional Physical Models an Analytical Aspect |url=http://jaac.xml-journal.cn/en/article/doi/10.11948/20220096 |journal=Journal of Applied Analysis & Computation |language=en |volume=13 |issue=3 |pages=1255–1273 |doi=10.11948/20220096 |issn=2156-907X|doi-access=free }}</ref>

<math display="block">A = \{f(t) : \ni M, p ,q> 0 , |f(t)|\leq M \exp(1/u) \}</math>

where  <math> p \leq u \leq q </math>, the Sumudu transform is defined as

<math display="block">S[f(t)]= \frac 1 u \int_0^\infty f(t) \exp\left(-\frac tu\right) \, dt </math>

== Relationship with other transforms ==
Sumudu transform is related to  [[Laplace transform]] by the following relation:
<math>S[f(t)](u)=\frac{1}{u} L[f(t)](\frac{1}{u})</math>;
and to Elzaki transform by the following relation:
<math>u^2S[f(t)](u)= E[f(t)](u)</math>.
